Real diff.stat is only 187 insertions/72 deletions across 79 files (a mechanical .m -> .mm rename plus a handful of podspec/include-path edits), but ctx.md renders 49013 tokens across 140 files because non-tree-sitter-friendly file types (Ruby podspecs, .mm) collapse into a single 'chunk' fragment spanning the entire file, so a 1-line podspec edit drags in a 124-line full dump, and a renamed .mm file with a tiny header tweak drags in its full 387-line body. The 1001-1480 line dump of the generated Podfile.lock is pure noise with zero semantic value for a reader. File-level selection recall is good (renamed files are all listed) but content-level precision is poor: comprehension-per-token is far below what a rename-focused diff should need.

Recall is good since the touched build files legitimately need cross-referencing to understand the merge, but precision suffers from full-file rather than hunk-scoped rendering.
